correctness.rationale: On a positive facet only the derivative of the fixed-coordinate column survives, since otherwise it duplicates the homogeneous column. The vector of complete derivative minors is, up to row signs, the exterior product of the affine columns with the restricted radial label. The n affine columns are orthogonal of squared norm N=2^(n-1); removing the affine component of the last column therefore gives squared norm N^n times the squared residual. On the even domain restriction to a positive facet chooses one representative of each antipodal pair, so its Gram normalization is 1/2 on counting measure. Distinct even characters restrict to distinct orthogonal characters; the constant is always removed, a quadratic character survives on n-2 facets, and a higher even character survives on n facets. Thus the Gram levels are (n-2)N^n/2 and nN^n/2 with precisely the stated multiplicities and equality space. For n=3 only the lower band exists, with Gram eigenvalue 32 and character output energy 256. Square roots give the claimed condition numbers.
residual_risks: Changing the choice or weighting of minors or changing the domain norm changes the numerical spectrum. The audit is analytic, not a formal certificate.

evidence: Himmelmann, Schulze and Winter impose both edge-length and face-planarity constraints on vertex first-order motions and discuss flexibility of the regular cube in that setting.
Jiménez Cuevas diagonalizes the Euclidean complete-minor form but leaves its general coefficients unevaluated.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A result on rank or flexibility for the joint constraints on unrestricted vertex motions is not a norm-sensitive numerical theorem for the complete minor map on even radial labels. Standard Cauchy–Binet is an ingredient, not a general spectral theorem on those labels.

evidence: Prior positivity and Walsh diagonalization alone do not give the values of the two levels, their ratio, or the equality classification for the sharp lower bound.
The missing quantitative computation is the complete-minor norm via the affine projection and the count of positive facets on which each Walsh mode survives.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The n=3 energy and constant kernel are covered; the normalization-sensitive all-dimensional evaluation is not supplied by the previously established structure.

value.rationale: This evaluates a natural stability constant for a previously defined geometric measurement whose general coefficients were left unspecified. It identifies the least detectable nonconstant radial modes and proves near-equal nonzero singular values in high dimension. This is useful for the specified linearized Euclidean map without claiming a nonlinear Mahler estimate or invariance under different row weights.
residual_risks: Value is for the complete positive-facet linearized map only, not for general polytope flexes or nonlinear stability.
